questions.question: If a spill occurs from a tank vehicle you are operating, what could happen?

options.text: You may have to pay for the cleanup.
You will not pay if someone else loaded the tank.
You must tell the local conservation department.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have to pay for the cleanup.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive a leaking tank. If you do, you may have to pay for cleanup costs.

questions.question: What license do you need to drive a vehicle that carries hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a passenger endorsement.
A CDL with an air brake endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials, even if it is not carrying them at the time.

questions.question: Where are fire extinguishers and other emergency equipment required?

options.text: Only in vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must carry emergency equipment, including fire extinguishers.

questions.question: What should you do when refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before refueling. Someone must stay at the nozzle to control fuel flow.

questions.question: What happens to your speed when driving down a hill?
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls your vehicle down a slope, making your speed increase.

questions.question: What should you consider when loading liquid cargo?

options.text: The air pressure in the tires.
The speed limits on the route.

questions.explanation: You must consider the weight of the liquid, how much it will expand, and legal weight limits when loading your tank.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles can enter.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is there.
Do not use a turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is there.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to react if you did not see them.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not grease the fifth wheel plate properly?
questions.explanation: Without proper lubrication, friction builds up between the tractor and trailer, causing steering problems.

questions.question: How can you prevent your tires and engine from overheating in hot weather?
questions.explanation: Driving faster creates more heat in your engine and tires. Driving slower in hot weather helps prevent overheating.

questions.question: Why can opening trailer doors during a cargo fire make it worse?

options.text: It lets oxygen in, which makes the fire spread.
It changes the temperature inside the trailer.
It adds moisture to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets oxygen in, which makes the fire spread.
questions.explanation: Opening trailer doors gives the fire oxygen, which can make it flare up and spread.

questions.question: Front tire tread depth in the main grooves must be at least:
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every main groove. Other tires need at least 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Steer with one hand and keep the other hand free

questions.explanation: Always follow the posted speed limit in work zones. Slow down if road or weather conditions are bad. Slow down even more if workers are present.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor that travels faster than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. These are hard to operate and require careful driving.

questions.question: One way to prevent hydroplaning on wet roads is to:

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth
Let air out of your tires

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your tires with good tread depth
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning risk increases if tire pressure is too low or tread is too worn. If you start to hydroplane, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:
questions.explanation: A rollover happens when a driver changes lanes or turns too quickly.

questions.question: A flare is required emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: During vehicle inspection, check for required safety equipment. This includes warning devices for parked vehicles, fuses, and liquid burning flares.

questions.question: Containers of hazardous materials must be:

options.text: Secured to prevent movement during transport

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured to prevent movement during transport
questions.explanation: Hazardous material containers must be secured so they will not fall, slide, or bounce during transport.

questions.question: ABS allows you to:
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup during hard braking. You should drive and brake the same way with or without ABS.

questions.question: After a vehicle starts, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes
Should turn off within a few seconds
Should stay on until you turn them off

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off right away after starting the engine. If a light stays on, the vehicle likely has a problem.

questions.question: After starting a trip, how soon must you check cargo securement?
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting your trip, within the first 50 miles, and every three hours or 150 miles after that. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safely secured the entire trip.
